reason: Ranked feasible source changes ahead of proposals needing unavailable generated helpers or lacking evidence for a useful change. Transpose fusion directly tests the requested small-tile path, but it must count repeated A transposes and all timed data movement; benefit is uncertain and correctness risk is high. Loop-order and ZA reuse changes are also substantial traversal edits with high pointer-mapping risk. B-panel packing has added timed work and an unverified locality hypothesis. Prefetching is a smaller, distinct trial but has no supplied evidence of a cache bottleneck. The two-K control simplifications have limited expected headroom given the prior two-K and loop-scheduling results. Tail alignment has no reported misalignment failure and should be dropped if the assembly already supports unaligned addresses. A transpose fusion applies only to the general fallback as proposed and does not directly improve the n=512 target. Panel64 needs an unavailable validated helper; transpose fusion’s repeated work and cost must be evaluated in full-call measurements. No proposal has measured evidence of improvement.
